ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The horizontal axis of the mass spectrum is mass number, marked at about 19, 20, 21, 22, and other positions; the vertical axis is percent abundance. In the figure there is a highest peak at mass number 20, with an abundance of about 90%. At mass number 21 there is a very small peak, with abundance close to 0% to 1%. At mass number 22 there is a smaller peak, with abundance of about 10%. Reasoning: These peaks represent the natural isotopes of the same element, whose main isotope has mass number 20, and it has small amounts of isotopes with mass numbers 21 and 22. The element that naturally exists and has Ne-20, Ne-21, Ne-22, with Ne-20 as the main isotope, is neon. Therefore the element is Ne.

raw_record.question_text: A mass spectrum of a naturally occurring sample of an element is shown above. What is the element?

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: identify the major spectral lines and their approximate percent abundances, especially the dominant line at mass number 20 and minor lines at 21 and 22. Then interpret these as the naturally occurring isotopes of a single element. Look up or recall which element has isotopes at masses 20, 21, and 22 with Ne-20 as the dominant isotope. This isotope pattern matches neon, so the element is Ne.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：质谱图的横轴是质量数，标出了约 19、20、21、22 等位置；纵轴是百分含量。图中在质量数 20 处有一个最高峰，丰度约为 90%。在质量数 21 处有一个很小的峰，丰度接近 0% 到 1%。在质量数 22 处有一个较小峰，丰度约为 10%。
推理：这些峰表示同一种元素的天然同位素，其主要同位素质量数为 20，并有少量质量数 21 和 22 的同位素。天然存在且具有 Ne-20、Ne-21、Ne-22，并且 Ne-20 为主要同位素的元素是氖。因此该元素是 Ne。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct isotope-pattern identification route: it uses the observed m/z peak positions and relative abundances, then matches them to known natural isotopic abundances. With only one spectrum and an open identification question, this is the main genuinely distinct method.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the mass spectrum axes and peaks: percent abundance on the y-axis, mass/charge values around 19–22 on the x-axis, with a very large peak at about 20, a tiny peak near 21, and a smaller peak near 22.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt statement that the image is a mass spectrum of a naturally occurring sample of one element and that the task is to name the element.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that a mass spectrum of a monatomic elemental sample shows peaks at the masses of its naturally occurring isotopes, with peak heights proportional to isotope abundances. Compare the pattern to periodic-table isotope data: neon has stable isotopes Ne-20, Ne-21, and Ne-22, with Ne-20 overwhelmingly most abundant and Ne-22 much smaller.
